Show, list and copy table styles

Source: R/tables.R
jstyle.Rd

A style holds a table's look and a journal's or a report's conventions: the font, the caption's form, the rules, the decimals, and for each table type its columns and labels. jstyle() lists the styles jstats can find; jstyle("myjournal") prints every setting the style gives, marking each one it takes from another style; and jstyle("apa", save.as = "myjournal") saves a copy as a style file, myjournal.jstyle, every setting written out with a note on what it does, to edit in any text editor (the step SPSS calls "Save TableLook As").

Usage

jstyle(style = NULL, save.as = NULL, overwrite = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

style

The style's name in quotes, or a path to a style file; NULL (the default) lists the styles, or with save.as copies joptions(style = ).

save.as

A name for the copy, in quotes: written as <name>.jstyle in the style folder when one is set, else in your jstats folder (tools::R_user_dir("jstats")), or to a path given with a folder.

overwrite

Logical. Replace a style file that exists? With FALSE (the default) an interactive session asks, and one that cannot ask stops.

...

Not used. An input jstyle() does not take stops with "unused input".

Value

Invisibly: the styles found (a data frame of name and path), the style, or the path of the file written.

Details

A style file is plain text: a setting is a name, an equals sign and a value; a # starts a note; the general settings come first, then one section per table type, [descriptives] and [frequencies]. A setting the file leaves out comes from the style its based.on line names. jstats looks for a style named in a call in the style folder (joptions(style.dir = )), the working directory and your jstats folder, in that order.
